How to pair with my TV / device

Quick pairing: press and HOLD the PS/home button for a second — the ring around it pulses white while your phone is visible, and turns solid green once connected.

PocketPad works with anything that accepts a Bluetooth gamepad: Smart TVs, phones, tablets, PCs — and the emulators running on them.

Samsung TV: Settings → Connection → External Device Manager → Input Device Manager → Bluetooth Device List (or Settings → Sound → Bluetooth Device List on some models).
Phone/tablet/PC: open its Bluetooth settings and scan for new devices.

1. In PocketPad: tap “Make phone discoverable”.
2. On the other device, select the name of your phone and confirm pairing on both screens.
3. Once paired, it connects to PocketPad as a gamepad. Next time, use “Connect to a paired device” to reconnect instantly.

Emulators (RetroArch etc.): PocketPad shows up as a normal gamepad — map the buttons once in the emulator’s input settings.

PS3 controller: plug it into the phone with a USB‑C OTG adapter. PocketPad detects it automatically and forwards its buttons and sticks alongside the touch controls.

IMPORTANT after updating to 2.2: un-pair PocketPad on your TV and pair again. A TV memorises what a controller can do when it first pairs, so the new analog triggers and corrected button numbering only take effect after a fresh pairing.

Xbox Cloud Gaming: switch “Controller style” to Xbox so the buttons read A/B/X/Y. The signals are identical either way — the host reads them by position (bottom/right/left/top), so only the labels change.

Start / Select: on the PlayStation style these are OPTIONS and SHARE; on the Xbox style they are MENU and VIEW.

Tip: switch to Super Nintendo, NES or Game Boy for retro games — same connection, different pad.

PocketPad also needs the \"Nearby devices\" permission to make your phone discoverable. Without it the controller still works with devices you already paired, but no new device can find it.

Touch shooter style:

A phone-style layout for games played on a TV or PC — a movement stick that appears wherever your left thumb lands, and a camera area covering everything not under a button, so your right thumb can look around by dragging.

The buttons are named by what they do (FIRE, AIM, JUMP, BUILD) rather than by a pad’s letters, but they send ordinary gamepad buttons. Set the game’s own controller bindings to match: FIRE is the right trigger, AIM the left trigger, JUMP the bottom face button, CROUCH the right face button, USE the left face button, SWAP the top face button, SPRINT the left stick click, BUILD the left shoulder, EDIT the right shoulder, and the four quick slots are the d-pad directions.

Two honest limits:

Dragging to look is NOT the same as it is on a phone. A drag tells a phone game how far to turn; a gamepad stick can only say how fast to keep turning. PocketPad turns how quickly your finger moves into how far the stick is pushed, which plays well but feels softer for small, precise aiming. No Bluetooth gamepad can do better than this.

PocketPad cannot see the game. There is no connection back from the TV or PC, so it has no way to know what you are standing over, what is in each slot, how much ammo is left, or whether you are building. Buttons that appear only when they are useful on a phone are always on screen here, and the slots are numbered rather than showing your actual items.

Move buttons works in this style too, and its layout is saved separately from the other styles.

PC (Windows 10/11) and tablets:

1. In PocketPad: tap “Make phone discoverable”.
2. On the PC: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Add device → Bluetooth, pick your phone, and confirm the code on both screens.
3. Back in PocketPad: Settings → “Connect to a paired device” → pick the PC.

Step 3 is not optional. A PC that pairs with a phone files it away as a phone and never goes looking for a controller on it, so the phone has to open the controller connection itself. If the PC refuses, PocketPad now says so instead of sitting on “connecting”.
